messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P0 alert — euw1: ELB connection resets + Route53 latency spike. Multiple services reporting 5xx increase. Paging oncall-nyc :phone:
oncall-nyc: I see alerts, joining. What's the observed customer impact?
sre-alex: Checking dashboards now — 5xx rate jumped from ~0.6% to 28% across the ELB fronting api-backend in eu-west-1. Latency at edge also up. Graphs: 50% of errors are connection resets, not app 500s.
eng-ops-jordan: Running quick health checks on ELB targets
eng-ops-jordan: ```bash
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-west-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-api/abcd1234
```
infra-bot: Target health summary: 18/24 targets UNHEALTHY, majority in euw1-azb. HealthReason: ConnectionReset/Timeout.
sre-alex: Logs show ENI detach/re-attach events in azb, and a small burst of packet drops from host-level metrics. Possible host networking instability in azb.
oncall-nyc: Any Route53 or edge indicators?
sre-alex: Route53 health checks for the edge are failing intermittently; seen an increase in resolver latency and NXDOMAIN spikes for ~2% of queries hitting euw1 resolver pool.
pm-lee: Customer-impact note: APdex violations for North/EU customers, some sessions failing to establish. CS reporting escalations from two enterprise customers.
oncall-nyc: Ok, immediate mitigation options: 1) Shift Route53 weights away from euw1 to euw2 fallback region. 2) Reduce Route53 TTL to speed cutover. 3) Force drain unhealthy targets and mark AZ as draining for ELB. Thoughts?
eng-ops-jordan: Recommend short TTL change to 60s and weight shift 70/30 to euw2. I'll prepare change set.
sre-alex: +1. Also open support ticket with AWS for azb hypervisor/ENI issues.
eng-ops-jordan: Preparing Route53 change batch:
```json
{
  "Comment": "temporary failover to euw2",
  "Changes": [
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "api.redwood-example.com.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "euw1-primary",
        "Weight": 30,
        "TTL": 60,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "1.2.3.4"}]
      }
    },
    {
      "Action": "UPSERT",
      "ResourceRecordSet": {
        "Name": "api.redwood-example.com.",
        "Type": "A",
        "SetIdentifier": "euw2-fallback",
        "Weight": 70,
        "TTL": 60,
        "ResourceRecords": [{"Value": "5.6.7.8"}]
      }
    }
  ]
}
```
eng-ops-jordan: Applying change via `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id ZZZZZ --change-batch file://failover.json`
infra-bot: Route53 change submitted, change ID: C0A1B2C3. TTL updated to 60s for the record.
pm-lee: Noted — inform CS and affected customers about traffic shift and expected DNS propagation ~2-5 minutes.
cust-success-emma: Messaging draft posted in #customer-notify: "We are routing traffic to alternative region due to regional networking instability in EU-West-1. Minimal downtime expected; mitigating now." Please review.
sre-alex: Meanwhile, on ELB/hosts: we're marking targets in azb unhealthy and letting ASG replace a subset to test host recovery. Running: `aws autoscaling set-instance-health --instance-id i-abc123 --health-status Unhealthy` for 6 instances.
eng-ops-jordan: Rolling replacements started. Monitoring connection reset rate — initial drop from 28% -> 12% within 120s for traffic answering from euw2.
oncall-nyc: Any signs of DNS caches still sending to euw1 heavily?
sre-alex: We see residual traffic to euw1 for clients honoring older TTL, but weight shift reduced overall error rate by ~60%. Error budget still impacted but improving.
eng-ops-jordan: AWS Support case opened (case #123456789) — they confirm networking instability in azb, possibly related to a hypervisor-level update failing on a subset of hosts. They recommend continued traffic redirection and host replacement.
pm-lee: Decide: keep weight at 70/30 for next 30 minutes, then reassess. Major customer sessions should be stable. Any objections?
oncall-nyc: No objections. Start handoff timer — I'll stay until seeding looks steady then hand to oncall-ldn.
eng-ops-jordan: Adding temporary firewall rule on the host to drop malformed SYN bursts we observed: ```iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --syn -m limit --limit 500/s -j ACCEPT``` (rolling).
sre-alex: Note: app-level retries were amplifying perceived impact; we throttled retry budget at loadbalancer edge to reduce load.
infra-bot: ELB target counts healthy now 20/24 healthy. Connection resets down to 4%.
oncall-nyc: 30m check-in: error rate steady at 1.5% globally, euw1 at 4%. Customer-impact alerts cleared in pager.
cust-success-emma: Customer notifications updated with status: "Mitigation in progress, traffic shifted to euw2, engineers monitoring. No action required from customers."
oncall-nyc: Preparing Handoff to oncall-ldn — summary: root cause likely networking/ENI/hypervisor instability in euw1-azb causing ELB target connection resets and Route53 health failures. Mitigations applied: Route53 weight shift (70/30), TTL lowered to 60s, unhealthy targets drained/replaced, ASG rolling replacements, retry throttling. AWS Support case opened. Current status: error rate near SLO, monitoring for regressions.
oncall-nyc: @oncall-ldn you're up. Full notes in incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2509876543
oncall-ldn: Taking over. Thanks — I'll run another pass on host replacements and keep weights at 70/30 for 30 more minutes, then plan gradual return to 100% when AWS confirms host region stability.
sre-alex: We've scheduled a follow-up with AWS for a deeper RCA once case closes. Please preserve logs for 30 days.
eng-ops-jordan: Final note — if any customers still see errors after 10m, escalate to PMs for bespoke reroute.
incident-bot: Incident P0 acknowledged by oncall-ldn. Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. :white_check_mark:
